title: Noetherian algebraic-space pseudo-coherence criterion
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use algebraic spaces over $S$ with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], quasi-coherent modules [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and canonical module functors [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Derived tensor and pullback use K-flat resolutions with flat terms; derived direct image uses K-injective resolutions. Noetherian means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally Noetherian on etale scheme charts. Coherent means quasi-coherent and, on Noetherian affine etale charts, associated to finitely generated modules. Let $Y$ be Noetherian and $K\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$ have quasi-coherent cohomology. A strictly perfect complex is bounded with terms direct summands of finite free structure modules. Call $K$ pseudo-coherent when for every integer $m$, locally on every etale site object, there is a strictly perfect $P$ and a map $P\to K$ inducing cohomology isomorphisms in degrees greater than $m$ and a surjection in degree $m$. Then $K$ is pseudo-coherent if and only if all $H^i(K)$ are coherent and $H^i(K)=0$ for all sufficiently large $i$.

source.place: Tag 08IK (lemma-identify-pseudo-coherent-noetherian), final equivalence; pseudo-coherence convention sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08FT (definition-pseudo-coherent).

proof.text: For an etale scheme chart $u:U\to Y$, restriction is localization on the small etale site by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. It is exact: kernels restrict sectionwise, and a section of the target of an epimorphism lifts on a covering, which remains a covering on the slice. Thus $H^j(K|_U)=H^j(K)|_U$. Quasi-coherence restricts because the local presentations of [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] remain local presentations after localization. The local approximation condition defining pseudo-coherence restricts as well. Conversely, if it holds on a covering of every site object, compose the coverings with the coverings giving the approximations; for each fixed $m$ this is exactly the condition in the item. Vanishing of a module sheaf is also detected on any surjective etale atlas: pull that atlas back to a site object and use the sheaf uniqueness axiom on the resulting covering.

source.place: Tag 08IK, first reduction paragraph; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08FT, definition-pseudo-coherent, and lemma-pseudo-coherent-independent-representative (3).

proof.text: Fix any affine etale chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$. By the locally Noetherian chart hypothesis $U$ is locally Noetherian, so [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], applied to the whole affine open of $U$, makes $A$ Noetherian. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization] to the quasi-coherent-cohomology object $K|_U$: choose $M_U\in D(A)$ and $a_A(M_U)\simeq K|_U$. This equivalence has no boundedness hypothesis. Its exactness and cohomology comparison give $H^j(K)|_U\simeq a_A(H^j(M_U))$, and its faithfulness detects zero modules. With the chartwise definition of coherence in the statement, $H^j(K)$ coherent implies $H^j(M_U)$ finitely generated: on this chart the sheaf is $a_A(N)$ for a finite $A$-module $N$, and applying sections and $\Gamma(U,a_A(-))\cong\mathrm{id}$ identifies $H^j(M_U)$ with $N$. Conversely, finite generation of these modules on every such chart is precisely coherence of $H^j(K)$.

source.place: Tag 08IK, reductions to an affine chart and to schemes; Tag 071Q, lemma-derived-quasi-coherent-small-etale-site; spaces-cohomology.tex Tag 07UB, lemma-coherent-Noetherian.

proof.text: The functor $a_A$ in step 2 is Zariski tilde followed by $\epsilon_U^*$. Choose any cochain representative of $M_U$ and let $E_U$ be its termwise associated Zariski module complex. Then $\epsilon_U^*E_U\simeq K|_U$ by the specified construction of [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization]. By [lem-sfb-etale-pseudocoherence-descent], $K|_U$ is pseudo-coherent in the strictly-perfect approximation sense defined in the statement if and only if $E_U$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent on the Zariski site for every $m$. By [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], this is the same as pseudo-coherence of $E_U$ in the sense of that node, local bounded-above finite-free models on $U$. By [lem-pc-affine-pseudo-coherent-criterion], the latter holds if and only if $M_U$ has a bounded-above finite-free representative. By [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], that is exactly pseudo-coherence of $M_U$ over $A$. All comparisons are invariant under the displayed derived isomorphisms; they concern ordinary unbounded module derived categories, not finite-coefficient constant sheaves.

source.place: Tag 08IK, second reduction paragraph; Tag 08HE, lemma-descend-pseudo-coherent; perfect.tex Tag 08E7, lemma-pseudo-coherent-affine.

proof.text: Assume $K$ is pseudo-coherent. For every affine etale chart, step 1 restricts this property and step 3 makes $M_U$ pseudo-coherent. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion] over the Noetherian ring $A$ from step 2. Every $H^j(M_U)$ is finite. The cohomology identification of step 2 therefore proves that every $H^j(K)$ is coherent according to the definition in the statement. This checks all degrees and all affine etale charts, without descending finite generation from one unspecified cover.

source.place: Tag 08IK, forward implication, reduced through perfect.tex Tag 08E8 to more-algebra.tex Tag 066E (2), lemma-Noetherian-pseudo-coherent.

proof.text: Still assuming pseudo-coherence, use quasi-compactness of $Y$ and [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas] to choose one surjective affine etale atlas $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$. Apply steps 2 and 3 to this chart. The same ring criterion [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion] supplies a single integer $b$ such that $H^j(M_U)=0$ for $j>b$. By the cohomology comparison in step 2, $H^j(K)|_U=0$ for these $j$. Step 1 detects zero sheaves on the surjective atlas, so $H^j(K)=0$ for every $j>b$. This is a global bound, not a family of bounds on a possibly infinite covering. If $Y$ is empty, the only module sheaf is zero and any $b$ works, so the assertion also holds in that case.

source.place: Tag 08IK, first paragraph: quasi-compact affine cover; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03H6, lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover; more-algebra.tex Tag 066E (2).

proof.text: Conversely, suppose all $H^j(K)$ are coherent and vanish for $j>b$. For each affine etale chart, step 2 gives a Noetherian $A$, finite $H^j(M_U)$ in every degree, and $H^j(M_U)=0$ for $j>b$ by faithfulness of $a_A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion] to obtain pseudo-coherence of $M_U$; step 3 then gives pseudo-coherence of $K|_U$. Any etale site object is a locally Noetherian scheme and is covered by affine opens. For each integer $m$, take its affine covering and then the local strictly perfect approximations just obtained on each affine. Composing these coverings proves the $m$-approximation condition defining pseudo-coherence on that object, as in step 1. Since $m$ and the object were arbitrary, $K$ is pseudo-coherent. There is no lower bound on its cohomology.
